output.description: Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has arrived at the Quezon City Jail, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology has said.
output.text:
Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has arrived at the Quezon City Jail, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology has said.

According to the BJMP, Romualdez arrived at the Payatas facility at 10:49 p.m.

He will undergo standard booking procedures: medical evaluation, fingerprinting, mugshot, interview, and orientation.

In a statement, the BJMP said Romualdez was placed in the jail infirmary.

"Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other [persons deprived of liberty] requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said.

The BJMP said the arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Sandiganbayan’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to.

Romualdez faces plunder charges over P7.2 billion in alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects.

His co-accused, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, and Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselin Sereño are all at large.

Other officials facing plunder before the Sandiganbayan who are detained at the QC Jail in Payatas include Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta. Also in the said jail is former Anak Kalusugan party-list Rep. Michael Defensor.

In a statement, Romualdez said he respects the Sandiganbayan’s decision.

“I have always said that I will face the charges against me and answer them before the proper court. That has not changed,” he said.

“I maintain my innocence. Haharapin ko ang kaso. Sasagutin ko ang mga paratang,” he added.

(I maintain my innocence. I will face the case. I will answer the allegations.)

He also extended his gratitude to the doctors.

The Sandiganbayan on Monday committed Romualdez to the male dormitory of the Quezon City Jail.

He had been in the hospital since his arrest. First, in the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, and then in the Philippine General Hospital.

Doctors from the PGH on Monday told the Sandiganbayan that his condition was stable enough so as not to require being confined in the hospital.

In its order dated September 14, the Third Division also set his arraignment on Wednesday, September 16.

"Accordingly, the court commits to the Quezon City Jail - Male Dormitory the living person of accused Romualdez, who is charged for the crime of plunder, to be held therein as a detention prisoner and as such, the accused shall not be moved, removed, transferred, and/or otherwise be released therefrom unless ordered by the court," the court said.

"The parties are reminded that the arraignment and pre-trial of this case as to accused Romualdez si set on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 8:30 in the morning," it added. –NB GMA News

Revoli Cortez, PPA pool/File MANILA—Malacañang maintained Tuesday that there should be no special treatment and that the law must be equally applied to all accused in the wake of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez's transfer to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas. Romualdez was moved to the QC jail on Monday night, hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer. Doctors of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital had found the former house speaker "clinically stable." READ: Martin Romualdez transferred to QC jail in Payatas Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said she has yet to talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. over his cousin's imprisonment. "Kahit po nasa kulungan sinuman, in general po, ito ating isasagot: Hangga't wala pa po kasing naibibigay na paghuhusga with finality ang isang korte, ang presumption pa rin po niyan ay inosente sila. Nagkataon lang po na ang mga kasong kinakaharap nila ay no bail, no bail recommended ang ibinibigay at sinasabi at pinag-uutos ng korte," she said in a press briefing Tuesday, September 15. "Kung ano po ang sinasapit ngayon ng mga diumanong sangkot, iyan naman po ay walang dapat sinisino – mayaman, mahirap, ordinaryong tao, may kapangyarihan. Kung nakagawa man ng mali sa taumbayan, kailangan lang din pong pantay-pantay kung ano po ang naranasan ng mga akusado," Castro added. "So wala pong dapat na special treatment. Hindi po kinakailangang mag-rally kung saan-saan para hindi mapanagot ang sinuman, dapat po pantay-pantay." Castro maintained that the Marcos administration is all for following the law and proper process of all accused regardless of their status. "Hindi kailangang umabuso, hindi naman kailangang kulang ang pagtrato sa maaaring nasasangkot. So, dapat lang po ay kung ano iyong naaayon sa batas at proseso," she said. Asked if Malacañang would encourage the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology to release more photos of Romualdez for transparency, Castro said it is up to the Bureau's discretion. "Nasa pamumuno na po nila iyan. Kung ano po ang nakikita nilang nararapat, as long na ang mga akusado ay nasa kustodiya po nila, nasa kanilang kamay na po ang pagpapasiya niyan," she stated. CANCELLED PGH VISIT Marcos was scheduled to have a visit to the Philippine General Hospital on Monday, September 14 but was cancelled Sunday night. Pressed why, Castro cited conflict in schedule with Marcos Jr. coming home from his participation in the recently concluded 18th BRICS Summit in India early Monday morning. "Kagagaling lang po kasi kagabi, madaling araw po dumating ang Pangulo. Alam ninyo naman po na halos mag-aalas singko na po dumating ang Pangulo. Hindi po naipagbigay—nabigay pabatid or nabigyan tayo ng kaalaman tungkol sa anong oras supposed to be kung pupunta man siya sa PGH, kasi kagagaling lang po niya sa India, kakatapos lang po ng kanyang trabaho at halos mag-aalas singko na po ng madaling araw dumating ang Pangulo," she said. The Palace official also denied that it had something to do with Romualdez who was then confined in the facility for an independent medical examination as ordered by the Sandiganbayan Third Division. "Wala. Walang napag-usapan patungkol diyan na iyon ang magiging dahilan. Nagkataon lang po siguro na kararating lang ng Pangulo, ng halos mag-aalas singko na po ng madaling araw, wala pa pong tulog iyon halos," she said. output.title: Martin Romualdez arrested over plunder charges, says DILG chief
output.description: Former Speaker Martin Romualdez has been served his warrant of arrest and has undergone the booking procedure at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic" Remulla said on Monday night.
output.text:
Former Speaker Martin Romualdez has been served with a warrant of arrest and has undergone the booking procedure at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic" Remulla said on Monday night.

According to Katrina Son's report on "24 Oras," Remulla said Romualdez was read the warrant and his rights in the presence of his lawyer.

A child of Romualdez was said to be in the room when he was served the warrant.

Remulla said the Leyte congressman is also being examined by doctors of the Philippine National Police and doctors from the hospital. They are expected to prepare a report for submission to the Sandiganbayan.

“He said Romualdez's condition will continue to be monitored until he is fit to be presented before the court.

Police have secured Romualdez at the San Juan hospital, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after suffering "a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack," Remulla said.

Remulla went to the hospital early Monday night with PNP chief Police General Jose Melecio Nartatez to serve on Romualdez the warrant of arrest the Sandiganbayan issued after the Ombudsman filed plunder charges against the Leyte congressman, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and two others.

He said Romualdez is considered a person deprived of liberty once he is read his rights.

"According to the doctors, he is suffering from a cardiovascular event. Unstable ang kanyang blood pressure and [he is] having an anxiety attack," Remulla said.

“However, we made it clear that, like in Secretary Bonoan’s case, we will check every day hanggang he’s well enough to be presented to court," he added.

“In the meantime, meron kaming armed guards outside his door. Meron kaming armed police outside the hospital and in the lobby," Remulla said.

P7.4B plunder charge

The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday filed a P7.4-billion plunder charge against Romualdez, former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Joselyn Tragua Serenio, who is the personal assistant of Romualdez, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.

“By repeatedly receiving, directly or indirectly, on at least 15 occasions, commissions, shares, percentages. kickbacks, "commitments." and/or other pecuniary benefits aggregating at least P7.4 billion by reason or on account of the respective public offices and positions of Romualdez and Co, including monies derived from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025, which monies were delivered to properties owned by, occupied by, or associated with Romualdez and received by Serenio and other persons acting for and in his behalf,” the criminal information read.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division hours later on Monday issued warrants of arrest against them.

"The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged," the Third Division said.

"Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested," it added.

Remulla said the hospital arrest was not a "permanent situation" for the former Speaker.

"But we assure you, we assure you, he cannot hide behind his wealth," Remulla said.

He said Romualdez's cell at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas is waiting if the Sandiganbayan would commit him to the detention facility.

Fair shake

A lawyer for Romualdez said he would face all allegations against him in connection with his alleged links to the kickback scheme involving the flood control mess.

“We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law,” Atty. Ade Fajardo, counsel of Romualdez, said in a statement.

“We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” he added.

He also said that Romualdez, a cousin of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr., only asked for a fair shake. –NB GMA News

output.title: SC, ICC on a collision course over case of ‘Tokhang’ survivor Efren Morillo
output.description: The Supreme Court is on a collision course with the International Criminal Court over the dismissal of a petition to review the case of Efren Morillo, an eyewitness and survivor of the war on drugs of former president Rodrigo Duterte, who has been detained at the Scheveningen facility while awaiting trial for charges of crimes against humanity in The Hague, Netherlands.
output.text: Ellen Tordesillas is president of VERA Files. A veteran reporter, she is the 1998 Marshall McLuhan fellow. Ellen Tordesillas is president of VERA Files. A veteran reporter, she is the 1998 Marshall McLuhan fellow. (Note: We have corrected the composition of the Supreme Court’s First Division after the High Court called our attention to the error. Dec. 6, 2025.) The Supreme Court is on a collision course with the International Criminal Court over the dismissal of a petition to review the case of Efren Morillo, an eyewitness and survivor of the war on drugs of former president Rodrigo Duterte, who has been detained at the Scheveningen facility while awaiting trial for charges of crimes against humanity in The Hague, Netherlands. The case of Morillo, lone survivor among five men in the August 2016 anti-drug Tokhang operations by the police in Payatas, Quezon City by playing dead, was cited by the ICC as “emblematic” of the extra judicial killings in its 2021 decision authorizing the investigation of Duterte’s war on drugs. But in a minute resolution on June 30, the Supreme Court First Division headed by Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo dismissed Morillo’s petition for certiorari for “for failure of the petitioners to sufficiently show that any grave abuse of discretion was committed by the Office of the Ombudsman.” The Office of the Ombudsman, then under Duterte appointee Samuel Martires, dismissed the case— filed by Morillo and the families of the four others killed during the Payatas Tokhang operations — for murder, frustrated murder, robbery, planting of evidence and grave misconduct. The four persons killed in the operations were Marcelo Daa Jr., Anthony Comendo, Jessie Cule and Rhaffy Gabo. The Gesmundo-led First Division is composed of Associate Justices Ramon Paul L. Hernando, Rodil V. Zalamea, Ricardo R. Rosario, and Jose Midas P. Marquez, all Duterte appointees. The CenterLaw, representing Morillo and the families of Daa, Comendo, Cule and Gabo, will file today (Dec. 5) a motion for reconsideration with a motion to elevate the case to the Supreme Court en banc, on the following grounds: Of the more than 30,000 cases of extrajudicial killings in the course of Duterte’s notorious drug war, the Morillo case stands out because he is one of the very few eyewitnesses who has survived. In its 2021 decision authorizing the investigation of Duterte’s war on drugs, the ICC cited: “The prosecutor puts forward as emblematic in this context the case of Efren Morillo. According to the available information, on 21 August 2016 in Payatas (Quezon City), Efren Morillo, a 28-year-old fruit and vegetable vendor, was detained at a house by plainclothes police officers, along with four friends, during an alleged Tokhang operation.” It continued: “The policemen pointed their guns at them, tied them up and later shot each of them, killing four. Efren Morillo was wounded but survived playing dead, and later gave an account of the incident. He in particular stated that he and his friends were frisked, handcuffed, and unarmed. The police, however, asserted that Efren Morillo and the others pulled their guns and shot at the police, to which the officers responded by shooting the suspects. According to the available information, Efren Morillo was subsequently charged with assaulting a police officer.” The Quezon City Metropolitan Trial Court has acquitted Morillo of the charges filed by the accused police officers, with a medicolegal doctor testifying that the trajectory of the bullet that hit him was downward, or execution style. In 2017, at the height of Duterte’s bloody war on drugs, the Supreme Court led then by chief justice Maria Lourdes Sereno granted Amparo protection to Morillo and the families of the four killed by prohibiting respondent police officers from entering within a one-kilometer radius from them. The Court of Appeals then decided to make the protection order permanent. Morillo together with the families of the four deceased victims, filed administrative and criminal charges before the Office of the Ombudsman for murder, frustrated murder, robbery, planting of evidence and grave misconduct against the policemen who attacked him and his friends. On March 22, 2024, after nearly seven years of preliminary investigation, the Ombudsman dismissed all the charges against the policemen, citing that the complainant failed to establish probable cause to indict them. The petitioners filed two petitions for certiorari on July 8, 2024: one before the Court of Appeals for the administrative charges and another before the Supreme Court for the criminal charges. The petition filed with the Supreme Court was premised on the ground that the Office of the Ombudsman committed grave abuse of discretion when it dismissed the criminal charges against the respondents for failure to establish probable cause. Last June 30, the Supreme Court First Division rendered its one-page decision dismissing the petition for certiorari for failure of the petitioners to sufficiently show that any grave abuse of discretion was committed by the Office of the Ombudsman. output.title: Inside Guo-Tok: How TikTok fan accounts whitewashed Alice Guo’s image amid POGO probe
output.description: A VERA Files investigation uncovered a network of 45 TikTok accounts that exhibited signs of a coordinated campaign from May to December 2024 to boost Guo’s reputation as a progressive leader and defend her innocence, amid the probe on her alleged links to illegal Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators (POGO) during this period.
output.text: By Nica Rhiana Hanopol, Rhenzel Raymond Caling, Psalm Mishael Taruc Editor’s Note: This story has been updated to reflect a more accurate attribution to a cited study and its authors. “What if she’s really innocent?” To online supporters of disgraced former Bamban mayor Alice Guo, the criminal accusations against their beloved leader are unbelievable. After all, how could a simple, people-loving and pretty-looking public servant who ushered her small municipality into a progressive one commit such crimes, they said. On TikTok, posts from fan accounts of Guo followed a curious pattern: identical captions and hashtags, similar video editing styles, uploaded within hours of each other, spreading the same messages. Guo, they claimed, was the best mayor Bamban ever had, yet she was the target of ruthless politicking. Guo has every reason to feel angry, they said. She is being publicly shamed in the Congress and labeled as a Chinese spy, despite all she did for her constituents. Detained in Pasig City jail, Guo is facing non-bailable qualified human trafficking charges, material misrepresentation, graft, 62 counts of money laundering, and three counts of falsification of deeds of sale documents, as of April 2025. Viral narratives about her on TikTok, however, either omitted or questioned these charges. It turns out, there is more to the story than meets the eye. A VERA Files investigation uncovered a network of 45 TikTok accounts that exhibited signs of a coordinated campaign from May to December 2024 to boost Guo’s reputation as a progressive leader and defend her innocence, amid the probe on her alleged links to illegal Philippine Offshore Gaming Operators (POGO) during this period. The network inundated TikTok with playful and trendy edits of Guo’s videos and photos in Bamban, reposting each other’s content and mimicking the behavior of K-pop fans in stan culture. They focused on her looks, mannerisms or antics, all while she was being grilled by lawmakers. In others, they reacted to news about Guo, bolstered her reputation as an “approachable” mayor, and curated “evidence” of her innocence. Most of the profiles appeared authentic, engaging with non-political content and posting selfies; but some carried foreign digital footprints typical of influence operations (IO). IO are orchestrated efforts to spread information – such as disinformation, propaganda and other harmful content in different formats – by various actors like governments, private groups or foreign interests to coerce or manipulate behavior and polarize society. Besides Guo, some of the accounts uploaded content idolizing other public figures like former president Rodrigo Duterte, his daughters Vice President Sara Duterte and Veronica “Kitty” Duterte (11), POGO-linked individuals Cassandra Ong and Shiela Guo (4) — even members of the Spanish royalty. A closer inspection of 19 accounts also revealed links to two Facebook (FB) groups run by Guo’s followers, including those who are not from Bamban, Tarlac. Gian Libot, a digital engagement specialist, said IO often uses multiple low-quality accounts (probably botted or bought) to reshare the same content, raising their visibility in the algorithm and creating an “artificial sense of widespread support.” “Reposting per se is not inherently wrong, it’s a typical marketing technique, but it becomes problematic because of the deception that happens when they use inauthentic accounts,” said Libot, who has worked on information integrity programs for international organizations. TikTok, a platform owned by the Beijing-based technology company ByteDance, defines covert IO as “coordinated, inauthentic behavior, where networks of accounts strategically work together to mislead people or […] influence public discussion.” This includes spreading the same narrative, using fake personas to pose as someone they’re not or attempting to shape public debate of social issues. The surge of TikTok posts about Guo came in June when the former mayor was suspended by the Ombudsman and was charged with qualified human trafficking by the Department of Justice. That same month, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) confirmed that Alice Guo’s fingerprints matched those of a Chinese national named Guo Hua Ping. During this period, the accounts mostly reposted Guo’s photos and videos from her FB page and YouTube channel, with glossy editing styles and captions gushing over her “cute” and “pretty” face. Others would go as far as to post fan cams — zoomed-in videos of an idol’s visuals, staple in K-pop stan culture. They would insert Filipino love songs like Maki’s Dilaw and TJ Monterde’s Palagi in videos from her appearances in the House or Senate hearings on illegal POGOs . They carved out Guo’s image as a do-gooder mayor, highlighting her achievements in Bamban such as providing financial assistance to students and granting the permit for the first-ever Jollibee branch in the municipality. Samuel Cabbuag, a digital sociologist and assistant professor at the University of the Philippines Diliman, said these types of content are designed to “hack the attention” of TikTok users and distract them from the real issues surrounding Guo. Cabbuag authored several research studies on digital influence cultures, including one on the political economy of covert influence operations in the 2022 Philippine elections. Although these are not necessarily disinformation posts, Cabbuag stressed that they help create the myth of Alice Guo as a “more humane person, emotionally complex and fighting for the truth.” Once that story has been laid out, he said, what all people are going to talk about is that , not the issues. Libot echoed this and said such content on TikTok can be persuasive that it may “easily make its way into average users and misinform them about nuances regarding Alice Guo’s case, and the credibility of the POGO operations.” For instance, the accounts went on a posting spree from late August to September, after Guo escaped to Malaysia and Singapore, and her subsequent arrest in Indonesia . VERA Files detected 12 accounts on Sept. 9 and 10 sharing similar videos of Alice hugging Shiela Guo before leaving the Senate, supposedly to display their close sibling relations. Two accounts reached significantly higher engagement than others and were posted within seconds of each other: But these videos omit an important context. On Aug. 27, Shiela admitted to having accompanied Alice to illegally depart the Philippines for Sabah by boarding several boats. In the same Senate subcommittee hearing, Shiela said she was not Alice’s biological sister . In a study published this year, Northwestern University PhD researcher Fatima Gaw and other digital media experts pointed out two types of political influencers on TikTok: “Stan” accounts, who portray politicians as “idols” and their supporters as “fans,” and “Trending” influencers, who stylize the politicians along with the vernacular taste on the platform. Guo seemed to benefit from both kinds, based on VERA Files’ analysis. All 45 TikTok accounts published fan edits and videos almost exclusively about the dismissed mayor, hiding their posts before 2024. More than half (24) of the accounts were created only last year, while 21 have been around as early as 2020, VERA Files found. Twelve of them were created from March to June, which coincided with the POGO hub raid in Bamban that led to a Senate resolution investigating Guo for alleged human trafficking and serious illegal detention. Twelve of the 45 TikTok accounts were created after the POGO hub raid in Bamban in March 2024. They bore Guo’s photos in their profile pictures from her 2022 campaign, her stint as mayor, and her appearances in committee hearings, even her casual selfies. Some of the photos have undergone minimal editing to change the background, add filters or other designs. Meanwhile, three-fourths (29) of the accounts played around with Guo’s name, such as her full name, last name or initials, in their usernames. Interestingly, VERA Files saw at least 40 usernames crop up on foreign websites as of January 2025: 20 were on Fansly, a pornographic content subscription service, and 13 were on Steemit, a United States-based blogging and social media website where users can earn cryptocurrency. But a visit to these links leads to non-existent pages. Disinformation experts say this likely indicates the use of a commercial service to generate multiple accounts – a strategy in affiliate marketing – suggesting that the motivations behind the accounts go beyond politics. One account @cyliceraxz stood out for posting fan content featuring Infanta Sofia of Spain and Leonor, Princess of Asturias, daughters of King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia of Spain. Created Oct. 24, 2022, it currently has 23,870 followers on TikTok. The Madrid-based news outlet El País previously reported about dozens of TikTok accounts impersonating Princess Leonor to promise financial aid in exchange for an initial payment of up to US$200. The scammer then pressures victims to pay additional fees until they run out of money. Using the open-source intelligence tool WhatsMyName.app , VERA Files found an account with the same username as @cyliceraxz on the Russian dating website dating.ru. The link directed to the application form of a user named Sergey, aged 58 and based in Chelyabinsk, Russia. WhatsMyName.app scours the internet to enumerate where a specific account username appears across a wide array of websites. In an email to VERA Files, El País reporter Pablo Canto Martinez said the account may be riding on the popular hashtags about the Spanish royal family “to gain visibility and engagement,” but it did not show signs of the same modus operandi he found. The first posts about the scam, Martinez said, appeared in October and peaked in November and December — the same months that @cyliceraxz posted about the Spanish princesses. As of April 29, @cyliceraxz has changed its default picture with Infanta Sofia’s photo holding a glass, originally taken from Getty Images in 2018. For Libot, this indicates that the TikTok accounts may be “part of a bigger operation, and not necessarily just focused on one candidate or personality.” He added, “In a more practical sense, it could also be that that’s the trendiest issue right now, so they are including themselves in the conversation to increase their visibility.” Four months after the POGO investigations ended, most of the TikTok accounts noticeably slowed down content creation with some shifting their attention to another political issue. An account, @alicia_guo2, has since renamed itself as @kittyduterte_guo and began posting content about Duterte’s youngest daughter on March 12, a day after the former president was arrested through a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court . The account is no longer accessible as of writing. Still, there are a few dedicated accounts that continue to cross-post content about Guo on TikTok and FB. Of the 45 accounts VERA Files monitored, 19 are part of FB groups called AeGis and Team ALG, whose names were derived from Alice Guo’s initials. AeGis has 15 members, boasting a total of 50 million engagements and 115,000 followers. They share similarly edited profile photos on TikTok — a group logo with each of their nicknames. Their FB group has been taken down as of this writing. Meanwhile, Team ALG, whose TikTok page was created on Oct. 23, 2024, claims to have about 65 members and has 4.20 million engagements on the platform. A number of the groups’ members claimed to be fans of Guo from other parts of the Philippines — not Bamban. Cabbuag explained that in any fandom, “you don’t have to be closely related or geographically located to support someone.” “As with any public figure, people can find some sort of relatability and some sort of connection to that person,” he said. AeGis’ and TeamALG’s content, however, do not end with innocuous posts “fangirling” over the former mayor. When Guo was ordered to transfer to the Pasig City jail along with eight other co-accused, at least 10 accounts bombarded TikTok from Sept. 20 and 25 with posts urging the Philippine National Police to return Guo to Camp Crame. Some of them jumped on the hashtag #NoToPasigCityJail, including five accounts linked with AeGis and TeamALG: @mayi.alg, @ihnahaliciaguo, @jen_00111, @jencfightforag, and @licia.there. While the posts were limited to 800 to 100,000 views, they amplified the same narrative: A “high-profile” personality like Guo did not deserve to be in the same cell as other persons deprived of liberty. In October, AeGis accounts tried to cast doubt on the authenticity of documents presented in the Senate probe, baselessly claiming that Guo’s fingerprint on her NBI clearance was “falsified.” The group also called out an article by The Straits Times in a Jan. 19 post , for supposedly using Guo as clickbait when it mentioned her links to Zhang Jie and Wu Duanren, who were under investigation in Singapore for a money laundering case. In Manila, Zhang is wanted by anti-organized crime and corruption authorities, while Wu is described as the “big boss” of illegal POGOs. With campaigning for the May 2025 local elections in its final stretch, some of Alice Guo’s TikTok fan accounts turned to being sentimental — reminiscing about her successful mayoral campaign in 2022 and regretting how her leadership was cut short after her supposed involvement in criminal activities surfaced. On April 14, one of the accounts posted clips of her giving away gifts to Bamban residents. “ Relapse malala. Kung hindi lang nangyari ‘to, siguro ikaw ulit ang magiging Mayor ng Bamban at siguradong wala kang kalaban ,” its caption read. (Having an extreme relapse. If only this didn’t happen, you would probably be the mayor of Bamban again and no one will challenge you [in the elections]). Despite being tucked away in prison miles from her town, Alice Guo remains present in Bamban. Her campaign slogan “ Asenso Garantisado ” (translated: “progress is guaranteed”), which was used over 3,000 times by this network of TikTok accounts, is mounted on top of the municipal hall. Across town, the same slogan is plastered on campaign posters of two rival mayoral bets — “ Ang Tunay Na Asenso Garantisado ” for a former mayor who supported Guo in 2022, and “ Kalmado Asenso Garantisado ” for a candidate whom she defeated last election. Residents believe it is a form of endorsement from Guo herself, who supposedly anointed these candidates to continue her promise of bringing progress and development into Bamban. And for some voters, this is exactly the kind of leader they are looking for. This story was published with the support of the Internews Indo-Pacific Media Resilience Program or IPMR. Gian Libot, a digital engagement specialist, said IO often uses multiple low-quality accounts (probably botted or bought) to reshare the same content, raising their visibility in the algorithm and creating an “artificial sense of widespread support.” “Reposting per se is not inherently wrong, it’s a typical marketing technique, but it becomes problematic because of the deception that happens when they use inauthentic accounts,” said Libot, who has worked on information integrity programs for international organizations. TikTok, a platform owned by the Beijing-based technology company ByteDance, defines covert IO as “coordinated, inauthentic behavior, where networks of accounts strategically work together to mislead people or […] influence public discussion.” This includes spreading the same narrative, using fake personas to pose as someone they’re not or attempting to shape public debate of social issues. The surge of TikTok posts about Guo came in June when the former mayor was suspended by the Ombudsman and was charged with qualified human trafficking by the Department of Justice. That same month, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) confirmed that Alice Guo’s fingerprints matched those of a Chinese national named Guo Hua Ping. During this period, the accounts mostly reposted Guo’s photos and videos from her FB page and YouTube channel, with glossy editing styles and captions gushing over her “cute” and “pretty” face. Others would go as far as to post fan cams — zoomed-in videos of an idol’s visuals, staple in K-pop stan culture. They would insert Filipino love songs like Maki’s Dilaw and TJ Monterde’s Palagi in videos from her appearances in the House or Senate hearings on illegal POGOs . They carved out Guo’s image as a do-gooder mayor, highlighting her achievements in Bamban such as providing financial assistance to students and granting the permit for the first-ever Jollibee branch in the municipality. Samuel Cabbuag, a digital sociologist and assistant professor at the University of the Philippines Diliman, said these types of content are designed to “hack the attention” of TikTok users and distract them from the real issues surrounding Guo. Cabbuag authored several research studies on digital influence cultures, including one on the political economy of covert influence operations in the 2022 Philippine elections. Although these are not necessarily disinformation posts, Cabbuag stressed that they help create the myth of Alice Guo as a “more humane person, emotionally complex and fighting for the truth.” Once that story has been laid out, he said, what all people are going to talk about is that , not the issues. Libot echoed this and said such content on TikTok can be persuasive that it may “easily make its way into average users and misinform them about nuances regarding Alice Guo’s case, and the credibility of the POGO operations.” For instance, the accounts went on a posting spree from late August to September, after Guo escaped to Malaysia and Singapore, and her subsequent arrest in Indonesia . VERA Files detected 12 accounts on Sept. 9 and 10 sharing similar videos of Alice hugging Shiela Guo before leaving the Senate, supposedly to display their close sibling relations. Two accounts reached significantly higher engagement than others and were posted within seconds of each other: But these videos omit an important context. On Aug. 27, Shiela admitted to having accompanied Alice to illegally depart the Philippines for Sabah by boarding several boats. In the same Senate subcommittee hearing, Shiela said she was not Alice’s biological sister . In a study published this year, Northwestern University PhD researcher Fatima Gaw and other digital media experts pointed out two types of political influencers on TikTok: “Stan” accounts, who portray politicians as “idols” and their supporters as “fans,” and “Trending” influencers, who stylize the politicians along with the vernacular taste on the platform. Guo seemed to benefit from both kinds, based on VERA Files’ analysis. All 45 TikTok accounts published fan edits and videos almost exclusively about the dismissed mayor, hiding their posts before 2024. More than half (24) of the accounts were created only last year, while 21 have been around as early as 2020, VERA Files found. Twelve of them were created from March to June, which coincided with the POGO hub raid in Bamban that led to a Senate resolution investigating Guo for alleged human trafficking and serious illegal detention. Twelve of the 45 TikTok accounts were created after the POGO hub raid in Bamban in March 2024. They bore Guo’s photos in their profile pictures from her 2022 campaign, her stint as mayor, and her appearances in committee hearings, even her casual selfies. Some of the photos have undergone minimal editing to change the background, add filters or other designs. Meanwhile, three-fourths (29) of the accounts played around with Guo’s name, such as her full name, last name or initials, in their usernames. Interestingly, VERA Files saw at least 40 usernames crop up on foreign websites as of January 2025: 20 were on Fansly, a pornographic content subscription service, and 13 were on Steemit, a United States-based blogging and social media website where users can earn cryptocurrency. But a visit to these links leads to non-existent pages. Disinformation experts say this likely indicates the use of a commercial service to generate multiple accounts – a strategy in affiliate marketing – suggesting that the motivations behind the accounts go beyond politics. One account @cyliceraxz stood out for posting fan content featuring Infanta Sofia of Spain and Leonor, Princess of Asturias, daughters of King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia of Spain. Created Oct. 24, 2022, it currently has 23,870 followers on TikTok. The Madrid-based news outlet El País previously reported about dozens of TikTok accounts impersonating Princess Leonor to promise financial aid in exchange for an initial payment of up to US$200. The scammer then pressures victims to pay additional fees until they run out of money. Using the open-source intelligence tool WhatsMyName.app , VERA Files found an account with the same username as @cyliceraxz on the Russian dating website dating.ru. The link directed to the application form of a user named Sergey, aged 58 and based in Chelyabinsk, Russia. WhatsMyName.app scours the internet to enumerate where a specific account username appears across a wide array of websites. In an email to VERA Files, El País reporter Pablo Canto Martinez said the account may be riding on the popular hashtags about the Spanish royal family “to gain visibility and engagement,” but it did not show signs of the same modus operandi he found. The first posts about the scam, Martinez said, appeared in October and peaked in November and December — the same months that @cyliceraxz posted about the Spanish princesses. As of April 29, @cyliceraxz has changed its default picture with Infanta Sofia’s photo holding a glass, originally taken from Getty Images in 2018. For Libot, this indicates that the TikTok accounts may be “part of a bigger operation, and not necessarily just focused on one candidate or personality.” He added, “In a more practical sense, it could also be that that’s the trendiest issue right now, so they are including themselves in the conversation to increase their visibility.” Four months after the POGO investigations ended, most of the TikTok accounts noticeably slowed down content creation with some shifting their attention to another political issue. An account, @alicia_guo2, has since renamed itself as @kittyduterte_guo and began posting content about Duterte’s youngest daughter on March 12, a day after the former president was arrested through a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court . The account is no longer accessible as of writing. Still, there are a few dedicated accounts that continue to cross-post content about Guo on TikTok and FB. Of the 45 accounts VERA Files monitored, 19 are part of FB groups called AeGis and Team ALG, whose names were derived from Alice Guo’s initials. AeGis has 15 members, boasting a total of 50 million engagements and 115,000 followers. They share similarly edited profile photos on TikTok — a group logo with each of their nicknames. Their FB group has been taken down as of this writing. Meanwhile, Team ALG, whose TikTok page was created on Oct. 23, 2024, claims to have about 65 members and has 4.20 million engagements on the platform. A number of the groups’ members claimed to be fans of Guo from other parts of the Philippines — not Bamban. Cabbuag explained that in any fandom, “you don’t have to be closely related or geographically located to support someone.” “As with any public figure, people can find some sort of relatability and some sort of connection to that person,” he said. AeGis’ and TeamALG’s content, however, do not end with innocuous posts “fangirling” over the former mayor. When Guo was ordered to transfer to the Pasig City jail along with eight other co-accused, at least 10 accounts bombarded TikTok from Sept. 20 and 25 with posts urging the Philippine National Police to return Guo to Camp Crame. Some of them jumped on the hashtag #NoToPasigCityJail, including five accounts linked with AeGis and TeamALG: @mayi.alg, @ihnahaliciaguo, @jen_00111, @jencfightforag, and @licia.there. While the posts were limited to 800 to 100,000 views, they amplified the same narrative: A “high-profile” personality like Guo did not deserve to be in the same cell as other persons deprived of liberty. In October, AeGis accounts tried to cast doubt on the authenticity of documents presented in the Senate probe, baselessly claiming that Guo’s fingerprint on her NBI clearance was “falsified.” The group also called out an article by The Straits Times in a Jan. 19 post , for supposedly using Guo as clickbait when it mentioned her links to Zhang Jie and Wu Duanren, who were under investigation in Singapore for a money laundering case. In Manila, Zhang is wanted by anti-organized crime and corruption authorities, while Wu is described as the “big boss” of illegal POGOs. With campaigning for the May 2025 local elections in its final stretch, some of Alice Guo’s TikTok fan accounts turned to being sentimental — reminiscing about her successful mayoral campaign in 2022 and regretting how her leadership was cut short after her supposed involvement in criminal activities surfaced. On April 14, one of the accounts posted clips of her giving away gifts to Bamban residents. “ Relapse malala. Kung hindi lang nangyari ‘to, siguro ikaw ulit ang magiging Mayor ng Bamban at siguradong wala kang kalaban ,” its caption read. (Having an extreme relapse. If only this didn’t happen, you would probably be the mayor of Bamban again and no one will challenge you [in the elections]). Despite being tucked away in prison miles from her town, Alice Guo remains present in Bamban. Her campaign slogan “ Asenso Garantisado ” (translated: “progress is guaranteed”), which was used over 3,000 times by this network of TikTok accounts, is mounted on top of the municipal hall. Across town, the same slogan is plastered on campaign posters of two rival mayoral bets — “ Ang Tunay Na Asenso Garantisado ” for a former mayor who supported Guo in 2022, and “ Kalmado Asenso Garantisado ” for a candidate whom she defeated last election. Residents believe it is a form of endorsement from Guo herself, who supposedly anointed these candidates to continue her promise of bringing progress and development into Bamban. And for some voters, this is exactly the kind of leader they are looking for. This story was published with the support of the Internews Indo-Pacific Media Resilience Program or IPMR. output.title: On cousins Martin Romualdez & Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
output.description: The arrest of former speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges.
output.text: The arrest of former speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges. That was a landmark event in the country’s history of the administration of justice. Never before in Philippine history has a former speaker of the House been charged and arrested upon the clearance of the president who happens to be his first-degree cousin. It has not been an easy move on the part of president BBM who is not known to be a violent or vengeful man but a compassionate and kind-hearted person. Not many expected that Romualdez would be charged with plunder, which is a non-bailable offense, aside from direct and indirect bribery and money laundering. That means that after his medical issues are properly addressed, he will be brought to the Quezon City detention center in Payatas to join the others, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, The arrest of Romualdez and his co-accused was based on the allegations that the former speaker allegedly received kickbacks and commissions on at least 15 occasions between 2022 and 2025. Prosecutors state he imposed a ?2 billion monthly quota on collections. The money was allegedly laundered through shell companies like Golden Pheasant Holdings, Bravos Holdings, and Valiant Consolidated Resource Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, born on November 14, 1963, is the third child of Madam Imelda Marcos' favorite brother Benjamin Kokoy Romualdez, former governor of Leyte and ambassador to the U.S. He is a graduate of UP Law, and Cornell and Harvard universities. He became a lawyer in 1993. He is married to Yedda Marie Mendoza Kittilstvedt who is also an incumbent member of Congress along with his son. Another son is a councilor of Tacloban. He was speaker from 2022 to 2025. Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr, or BBM, born on September 13, 1957, is the only son of the late Ferdinand Edralin Marcos Sr. and Madam Imelda. Since he has no brother, BBM is close to his male cousins including Ferdinand Martin. Incidentally, the former speaker's father, Kokoy, named him Ferdinand Martin in honor of Ferdinand Marcos who helped Kokoy become Leyte governor and U.S. ambassador. It pains BBM too much to have to allow the charges to be filed against his own esteemed first cousin, and it pains Martin even much more to be "betrayed" by his close relative. But it appears that the evidence calls for the charges to be filed. No one is above the law. There should be no selective justice. Let justice be done though the heavens may fall, so to say. If Kokoy were alive today, and if Madam Imelda were in her prime at these times, the two would have raised hell to prevent all this by all means. I have my own thesis also, that all this was also planned and cleared by the first lady who is a brilliant lawyer herself and a Law professor at that. The first lady is just trying to protect the administration of President BBM. Charging Martin is biting the bullet and crossing the Rubicon. There shall be no turning back. The link between the Marcoses and the Romualdez clan will never be the same again. What matters most is that such a draconian move is definitely good for the Filipino people. output.title: Romualdez inilipat na sa Quezon City jail, mugshot inilabas
output.description: Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement. Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes. Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects. Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez. Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan. Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency. Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga. Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez. output.title: Martin Romualdez transferred to QC jail in Payatas | ABS-CBN News
output.description: Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is now at the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas, after leaving the University of the Philippines-Philippine Gener
output.text: peaker Martin Romualdez delivers his speech as he steps down from his post as Speaker of the House of Representatives on Wednesday, September 17, 2025. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA ( 3RD UPDATE ) - Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was moved to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas on Monday night, September 14. A transport convoy by the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) departed from the Pedro Gil exit of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital in Manila shortly after 10:00 p.m. This comes hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer , with UP-PGH doctors finding Romualdez "clinically stable" and noting that he does not require continued hospitalization. Upon his arrival, intake protocols began immediately. The standard admission process that encompasses a medical evaluation, fingerprint acquisition, mugshot, interviews, and orientation is currently underway. They said Romualdez was committed to the Quezon City Jail–Male Dormitory at approximately 10:49 p.m. in compliance with the order of the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division. "Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other PDL requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said in a statement. "The arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Court’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to," it added. "The BJMP assures the public that it will remain professional, impartial, and consistent in the implementation of its rules and regulations. All PDL under its custody are treated fairly and humanely, without distinction or privilege based on status or position." PLUNDER CASE Romualdez was arrested last Monday, September 7, after the Sandiganbayan issued a warrant for the P7.4-billion plunder case filed by the Ombudsman. He was initially confined at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center before being transferred to UP-PGH on Saturday for an independent examination. READ: PGH finishing medical exams on Martin Romualdez Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, medical director of UP-PGH, took the witness stand on Monday during the Sandiganbayan Third Division's hearing on Romualdez's motion for continued confinement. When Associate Justice Ronald Moreno asked if Romualdez could be discharged from the hospital at any time, Legaspi answered in the affirmative. Romualdez is expected to stay in a cell that is about 50 square meters, with five double-deck beds. The BJMP said it was also considering Romualdez's medical condition and security concerns in determining his placement. Under BJMP policy, PDLs with certain medical or psychiatric conditions and comorbidities should not be left alone in a cell. Romualdez said in a statement on Monday that he respects the court's decision, but maintains his innocence . RELATED VIDEO: Leyte First st District Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez elected as the Speaker of the House of Representatives during the opening of the first regular session of the 20th Congress on July 28, 2025. Jonathan Cellona, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA (3rd UPDATE) — The Sandiganbayan on Monday ordered former House Speaker Martin Romualdez’s transfer to the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas from the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital (UP-PGH). The order came after UP-PGH doctors found Romualdez “clinically stable” and said he does not require continued hospitalization. Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, medical director of UP-PGH, took the witness stand during the Sandiganbayan Third Division’s hearing on Romualdez’s motion for continued confinement. PGH: Romualdez no longer needs hospital confinement Legaspi and his authorized representatives were ordered by Associate Justice Karl Miranda on Friday, Sept. 11, to conduct an independent medical examination of Romualdez to verify the findings and tests conducted by Cardinal Santos Medical Center, where he was initially confined. “We formed a team of 12 doctors all covering various conditions he (Romualdez) was diagnosed to be suffering from another hospital,” Legaspi said. When Associate Justice Ronald Moreno asked if Romualdez could be discharged from the hospital at any time, Legaspi answered in the affirmative. Romualdez underwent a dobutamine stress test, which stimulates the heart to contract. The test showed that he is at low risk of a heart attack. Legaspi said Romualdez has a 3 percent chance of suffering a heart attack every year within the next decade, which he described as “not very high.” He added that Romualdez continues to have chronic coronary syndrome, but their examination ruled out unstable angina, a condition in which the heart does not receive enough blood flow and oxygen. Legaspi also said there was evidence of a previous stroke, but Romualdez was not found to have suffered a new stroke. He said Romualdez’s Type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hypothyroidism are controlled but require continuous monitoring. He added that Romualdez has no acute cerebrovascular disease, although infarcts, or areas of tissue damaged by interrupted blood flow, were found. Meanwhile, Legaspi said their psychiatrist confirmed Romualdez’s diagnosis of major depressive disorder and anxiety. He said Romualdez needs continued psychiatric treatment, but not necessarily on an inpatient basis, since he has no grave inability to maintain basic self-care and does not pose a risk of suicidal harm. Romualdez was also found to have severe sleep apnea. Legaspi said he was recommended to use continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) during sleep and undergo regular follow-ups with a sleep specialist. Legaspi said these conditions can be managed outside the hospital. “’Yung aming multi-disciplinary team, inisa-isa namin ang mga sakit na ito at wala ni isa sa mga sakit na ito ang nangangailangan na nasa ospital para magamot. Pero kailangan pa rin mabigyan ng atensyon,” Legaspi told reporters during an ambush interview. “Kaya meron kaming kondisyon na pinakiusap sa korte para masiguro ang kanyang kaligtasan at kalusugan ay maibigay,” he added. Dr. Henry Fabro, a physician at the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), told the court that their facilities are sufficient for cardiac monitoring and have sockets for Romualdez’s CPAP machine. He added that 23 to 24 nurses are on duty around the clock at the Payatas Jail and are ready to bring Romualdez to the nearest hospital should the need arise. WHAT HAPPENS AFTER TRANSFER Once transferred to the jail, Romualdez will undergo the standard commitment and booking procedures, similar to other persons deprived of liberty (PDLs). He will undergo an interview, confiscation of unauthorized items, mugshot-taking, medical history checking, and cell assignment, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) said. “The plan is to transfer within the day. Dapat as soon as possible, yun ang instruction din sa ating BJMP personnel for public interest. Pangalawa pagdating niya sa jail dadaan siya sa standard operating procedure ng commitment at booking procedure,” BJMP spokesperson Jail Superintendent Jayrex Bustinera said. “May naihanda na tayong mga selda, at of course titignan natin depende sa lalabas na order kung may mga consideration doon,” he said. Each cell at the facility has a capacity of 10 PDLs. The cell prepared for Romualdez is about 50 square meters and has five double-deck beds. The jail currently houses more than 3,200 PDLs. The BJMP said it was also considering Romualdez’s medical condition and security concerns in determining his placement. Under BJMP policy, PDLs with certain medical or psychiatric conditions and comorbidities should not be left alone in a cell. Visitation at the facility is allowed from Tuesday to Sunday. The BJMP has yet to receive a list of individuals authorized to visit Romualdez. 'FACE THE CHARGES' In a statement, the Leyte congressman said he respects the court's decision "I have always said that I will face the charges against me and answer them before the proper court. That has not changed," Romualdez said. " I maintain my innocence. " Philippine General Hospital medical director Dr. Gerardo Legaspi testified earlier in the day that Romualdez’s continued inpatient confinement was not medically required as his risk of an impending heart attack is low based on their independent medical evaluation. Marcos denies Romualdez arrest is staged drama Legaspi said Romualdez’s chronic coronary syndrome remained present but his unstable angina has been ruled out. Romualdez’s condition can be managed outside the hospital, the PGH official said. Court orders BJMP: Take custody of Romualdez Legaspi also confirmed that Romualdez has major depressive disorder and anxiety, which need continued psychiatric treatment. However, Legaspi said the former House speaker is not in need of hospital admission because he has no grave instability to maintain basic self-care and he does not pose risk of suicidal harm. Dr. Henry Fabro — a physician at the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology, which has custody of Romualdez — also told the Sandiganbayan that their facilities are sufficient for cardiac monitoring. He said the Quezon City Jail in Payatas has around 24 nurses on duty around the clock. House of Representatives handout MANILA — The Philippine General Hospital (PGH) on Monday refuted claims that House Speaker Martin Romualdez stayed in a presidential suite. PGH medical director Dr. Gerardo Legaspi said Romualdez was brought to a large-capacity room that could accommodate medical tests and security personnel. “Ang aming basehan ng pagkuha ng kwarto sa kanya, una dapat secured… pangalawa, hindi siya maiistorbo ng mga pasyerte.
